correctness.rationale: Both half-bicone ray exits are exact and sum to f(|u1|)+f(|u2|). The support and all extremal directions follow from 1<=t+sqrt(1-t^2)<=sqrt(2). A uniform spherical chart has measure dtheta dz/(4pi). The four lower charts have coercive phi^2+z^4/4 normal form, yielding the beta integral and exponent 3/4. The six upper charts have respective limiting areas 2 and 4/3, leading to 7/(3pi) and marked mixture 3/7 versus 4/7; dominated indicator convergence proves total variation. The embedded Python-standard-library checker independently reconstructs rays and checks coefficients numerically; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: Directional chord extremes of a classical developable solid are natural metric quantities. The non-Morse quartic minimum causes a noninteger exponent 3/4, contrasted with the quadratic maximum tail. Six maximizing directions split into two geometrically different tangent classes with exact 3/7 and 4/7 weights. The exact CDF integral, two gamma/rational constants and conditional geometry are substantive, not a textbook parameter substitution.
